title: JavaScript Modules: ESM, CommonJS and Tooling
summary: Quick revision notes on ES modules versus CommonJS, import/export forms, dynamic import, live bindings, bundlers with tree shaking, the package.json type field and npm scripts.

chapters.title: Modules: The Mental Model
points: A module is a file with its own scope: top-level variables are private unless exported, and each module is evaluated once then cached
CommonJS (CJS): require() and module.exports, loaded synchronously at runtime; the default for .js in Node unless configured otherwise
ES modules (ESM): static import/export, parsed before any code runs; the language standard, works in browsers and Node
Comparison: CJS is dynamic and synchronous with exports as value copies; ESM is static and async-capable with live bindings, strict mode always, and no __dirname/__filename/require
Interview Point: Why can ESM be tree-shaken but CJS usually cannot? What does 'static analysis' mean for imports? Why is a module evaluated only once?

chapters.title: Import and Export Forms
points: Named export: export const a = 1; export function f(){}; import with matching names: import { a, f } from './m.js'
Default export: export default expr (one per module); import with any name: import Foo from './m.js'
Rename and namespace: import { a as b }, export { a as b }, import * as ns from './m.js' (namespace object is read-only)
Re-export and side-effect import: export { a } from './m.js'; export * from './m.js' (skips default); import './setup.js' runs the module only
Mistake: import { x } from './m' fails in Node ESM because file extensions are required; also braces vs no braces confuse default and named imports
Interview Point: Named vs default export trade-offs? What does export * not re-export? How do you import a default and named together (import d, { n } from)?

chapters.title: Live Bindings and Dynamic Import
points: Live binding: an imported name is a read-only view of the exporter's variable, so later changes in the exporting module are visible to importers
CJS exports are a snapshot: const { count } = require('./m') copies the value at that moment and never updates
Dynamic import(): returns a Promise of the module namespace, usable anywhere (inside if/functions) for lazy loading and code splitting: const m = await import('./x.js')
Top-level await works in ESM only; it blocks the importing modules until the promise settles
Circular imports: ESM gives uninitialised bindings (TDZ ReferenceError) while CJS gives a partially filled exports object; fix by restructuring or lazy access
Interview Point: What is a live binding and can an importer assign to it? How does import() differ from import statements? How do circular dependencies behave in ESM vs CJS?

chapters.title: Node Interop and package.json type
points: "type": "module" in package.json makes .js files ESM; "commonjs" (the default) makes them CJS; .mjs is always ESM and .cjs is always CJS
The nearest package.json to the file decides how .js is treated
ESM can import CJS (module.exports becomes the default import); CJS require() of ESM historically failed with ERR_REQUIRE_ESM, so use await import() from CJS
"exports" field maps public entry points and can offer conditions { import, require } for dual packages; "main" is the legacy fallback

Mistake: 'require is not defined in ES module scope' or 'Cannot use import statement outside a module' means the file's type is the wrong one; recreate __dirname with import.meta.url or import.meta.dirname
Interview Point: How does Node decide if a file is ESM? How do you load ESM from CJS? What is the exports field for?

chapters.title: Bundlers, Tree Shaking and npm Scripts
points: Bundler (webpack, Rollup, Vite/esbuild) resolves the import graph and emits optimised bundles, with code splitting at dynamic import() points
Tree shaking drops unused exports; it needs static ESM syntax, so CJS and dynamic require defeat it
"sideEffects": false in package.json tells bundlers that unused modules are safe to remove; list files with side effects (e.g. CSS, polyfills) in an array
npm scripts live in "scripts": run with npm run build; start and test need no 'run'; pre/post hooks (prebuild, postbuild) run automatically; node_modules/.bin is on PATH
Mistake: import * as lib or barrel files with side effects keep code in the bundle; pass args with npm run dev -- --port 3000; chain with && (sequential) and use a cross-platform tool for env vars
Interview Point: What breaks tree shaking? What does sideEffects do? Difference between dependencies and devDependencies in the build?

chapters.title: ESM and CJS Cheat Sheet
points: CJS: const x = require('x'); module.exports = {...}; exports.a = 1
ESM: import x from 'x'; import { a } from 'x'; export default v; export const a = 1
Extensions: .mjs = ESM, .cjs = CJS, .js follows package.json "type"
Dynamic and lazy: const m = await import('./x.js'); top-level await is ESM only
npm: npm run <script>, npm start, npm test, npm run x -- --flag, pre/post hooks; tree shaking needs ESM plus "sideEffects": false
Interview Point: Which module system would you pick for a new library and why? How do you ship a package that supports both?
